text.p: These are the main stories in Latvian newspapers on Tuesday. Prepared for Reuters by the Co-operation Fund. Reuters has not verified these reports and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Seventy-four illegal immigrants have left the Olaine refugee camp for Scandinavian countries and Australia which have agreed to give them asylum. There are still 47 illegal immigrants left in Olaine, 13 of them waiting for being given the status of refugees.

- The Latvian state-owned gas company Latvijas Gaze, which is scheduled for privatisation, has agreed on natural gas supplies with the Russian concern Gazprom for 1997. The gas price stays on the 1996 level, about $77.5/1000 cubic metre.
- Transportation Minister Vilis Krishtopans said he will affirm the new chief manager of the Riga Sea port, Andrejs Inkulis, only after evaluating his work programme.
- European Union experts have drawn a confidential report -- of which NTV and the Diena newspaper obtained a copy -- claiming there is corruption on all levels of the Latvian government.

- Representatives of Baltic States and Russia failed to agree on dividing the air space over the international waters of the Baltic Sea at a meeting in Paris last week. The main obstacles were differences between Latvia and Lithuania.

- The Bank of Latvia has sanctioned an increase of the main assets in five commercial banks. According to the central bank, the banking sector in Latvia shows two trends: growth of main assets and an increase of foreign investment in the commercial banks. During 12 months from the mid 1995 the total main assets of the Latvian commercial banlks increased to 82 million lats from 61 million.
- President of Lukoil, a Russian oil concern, Vagid Alekperov, will visit Latvia on December 18-19, to officially open Lukoil's eigth petrol station in Latvia.
- The Transport Ministry reported on its achievements in 1996 with the most important being the railway cargo turnover which has shown a 38 percent increase.
- Forty-two Latvian soldiers have left for Sweden to replace the first platoon of the Latvia peace-keeping platoon, stationed in Bosnia.
